tasks.description:
Build the archive primitives the any-size export and import need, in apps/community. No behaviour change to exports yet. No migration.

### Why
fflate 0.8.3 (the current export writer and P3's planned import reader) has no ZIP64: no archive over 4 GiB, no more than 65,535 entries. stageBlob (storage/blob-store.ts) stages every put to a local temp file (the S3 store too), with a 1 GiB export ceiling, and managed blob reservations must commit within one hour, so the archive must be written as bounded segments.

### Modules
1. `src/archive/zip64-writer.ts`: writes one SEGMENT of a ZIP64 archive as an AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>. API sketch:
   - `createSegmentWriter()` → `{ addDeflated(name, source), addStored(name, source), finish(): { bytes stream, entries: EntryRecord[] (structured: name bytes, CRC-32, method, compressed size, uncompressed size, offset RELATIVE to the segment start, DOS time/date), entryCount } }` plus `encodeEntriesIndex(entries): Buffer` / `decodeEntriesIndex(buf)` (compact binary, stored in export_segments.entries_index). Central-directory records are NEVER stored as bytes.
   - `writeTail({ segments: {byteSize, entries}[], tailEntries })`: writes tail entries (NDJSON files, icon, manifest.json last), then encodes the central directory from every segment's structured entries with absolute offsets (segment start + relative offset), then the ZIP64 end of central directory record, the ZIP64 locator, and the classic end record. The tail may be split across several blobs.
   - Every entry: UTF-8 name (flag bit 11), data descriptor (flag bit 3) because CRC-32 and sizes are known after streaming; ZIP64 data descriptor (8-byte sizes) when a size needs it. EVERY central-directory record ALWAYS carries the ZIP64 extended-information extra field (uncompressed size, compressed size, local-header offset) with the three 32-bit fields set to 0xFFFFFFFF, whatever the values (one record shape). Always emit ZIP64 end records. Method 8 via zlib.createDeflateRaw for NDJSON; method 0 for file bytes. CRC-32 via zlib.crc32 (Node 24).
   - A test-only option forces ZIP64 records on every entry.
2. `src/archive/segmented-source.ts`: a logical byte range over ordered blobs `{ key, byteSize }[]`: `size`, `read(start, endInclusive)` → stream, using one ranged BlobStore.get per blob touched.
3. `src/archive/zip-reader.ts`: reads any zip (fflate-written version 1 archives and our ZIP64 archives) through its central directory over a segmented source: find the end record in the last 64 KiB + 22 bytes, follow the ZIP64 locator, STREAM the central directory (do not hold all records), open entries by offset. Refuse: encrypted entries, methods other than 0/8, directory entries, names outside a caller-supplied allowed pattern, duplicate names (set of name digests), a local header whose name or sizes disagree with the central directory, overlapping entries, inflated output past the declared size by one byte. Never use a name as a filesystem path.
4. BlobStore: `get(key, { signal, range?: { start: number; end: number } })` (inclusive end). File-system store: read stream with start/end. S3 store: GetObject with `Range: bytes=start-end`, check the returned Content-Range. `byteSize` is the range length.
5. New put kind `export_segment`: accepts a first-bytes signature of a local file header (PK\x03\x04) or central directory header (PK\x01\x02) or ZIP64 end record (PK\x06\x06); ceiling 1 GiB; content type application/zip.
6. Add `yauzl` as a devDependency of @dorkos/community for cross-check tests only.

### Acceptance criteria
- Unit: local header, data descriptor (both sizes), central directory record (with and without ZIP64 extra), ZIP64 end record, locator, classic end record byte-exact against fixtures built from PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10; CRC-32 matches zlib.crc32 vectors.
- AC-2: every central-directory record carries the ZIP64 extra field (byte check). A three-segment + tail archive is read without error by yauzl, Info-ZIP `unzip -t`, `bsdtar -tf`, Python `zipfile` (`testzip()` is None), and on macOS runners `ditto -x -k`; a missing tool is skipped with a logged reason; CI installs unzip, bsdtar, python3. Also, with the force-ZIP64 hook, and separately with a synthetic stream of more than 65,535 entries and one logical offset above 4 GiB written to a null sink, yauzl reads the central directory and entry offsets correctly; our reader reads the same. Opt-in `COMMUNITY_EXPORT_BIG_TEST=1` writes and re-reads a real 5 GiB archive end to end.
- Three segments written independently and concatenated with a tail open in yauzl with every entry's bytes intact; rewriting the middle segment with a different size and rewriting only the tail still opens.
- The reader reads a real version 1 export (fflate) and refuses each tamper: encrypted flag, method 12, `../x` name when the pattern forbids it, duplicate name, local/central name mismatch, overlapping offsets, deflate bomb (inflates past declared size).
- Ranged get: first byte, last byte, and a middle slice correct on both stores (vitest.pg/vitest.s3 as appropriate).
- TSDoc on all exports; typecheck and lint pass.
tasks.subject: [community-export-any-size] [P1] Add the ZIP64 segment writer, central-directory reader, and ranged blob reads

tasks.description:
Make owner and personal exports background jobs that write a segmented ZIP64 archive with manifest version 2, with a resumable download (apps/community + packages/shared). Launch blocker. Depends on task 1.1 and member erasure 1.1 (#2029: community_content_versions, entry_redactions, erasure deleteExports). Migration: the next free number at build time.

### Today (routes/exports.ts)
The export runs inside POST /owner/export: snapshot() reads every collection with LIMIT 10,001 in one REPEATABLE READ transaction and answers 413 ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE above 10,000 rows, 1 GiB of files (MAX_EXPORT_BYTES) or a 16 MiB manifest; fflate Zip → blobStore.put(maxBytes 1 GiB); commit checks the content version; archive lives 1 hour; download has no Range and re-checks membership twice per chunk.

### Archive layout (one ZIP64 file stored as consecutive segments)
Data segment n: `entries/NNNNNN.ndjson` (deflated rows for a contiguous (channel_id, seq) range), `attachments/NNNNNN.ndjson` (metadata rows for those messages' files), then `files/<attachmentId>/<sanitizeDisplayName(name)>` (stored). Collection segments (kind 'collection', after the last data segment): channels/NNNNNN.ndjson, members/…, agents/…, channel-members/…, agent-channel-members/…, audit-events/… (owner/evidence only), each file at most 100,000 rows, each segment at most COMMUNITY_EXPORT_SEGMENT_BYTES. Tail (kind 'tail'): ONLY community/icon (if any, ≤25 MiB), manifest.json LAST (≤1 MiB), the central directory, and the end records; if the central directory needs more than one blob it is split only where a central-directory record or the ZIP64 end record starts, so every blob begins with PK\x03\x04, PK\x01\x02, or PK\x06\x06 (checked by the export_segment put kind). Stored entries of known size (attachments, icon; buffer ≤64 MiB) put CRC-32 and sizes in the local header with NO data descriptor (ditto refuses stored entries with a descriptor); deflated NDJSON entries use a data descriptor. Planner closes a data segment when estimated size (row JSON length + files' byte_size + header overhead) reaches COMMUNITY_EXPORT_SEGMENT_BYTES.

### Manifest version 2 (packages/shared/src/community-wire.ts)
```ts
export const CommunityExportManifestV2Schema = z.strictObject({
  version: z.literal(2), scope: z.enum(['personal','owner','evidence']), exportId: id,
  requesterMemberId: id.nullable(), createdAt: timestamp, completedAt: timestamp,
  community: z.strictObject({ id, name: z.string().min(1).max(80), description: z.string().max(1_000).nullable(),
    admissionPolicy: CommunityAdminAdmissionPolicySchema, lifecycle: z.enum(['active','archived']),
    lifecycleVersion: z.int().positive(), settingsVersion: z.int().positive(),
    icon: z.strictObject({ path: z.literal('community/icon'), contentType: z.string(), byteSize: z.int().positive(), checksum: z.string().regex(/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/) }).nullable() }),
  files: z.strictObject({ channels, members, agents, channelMembers, agentChannelMembers, auditEvents, entries, attachments }), // arrays of archive paths
  counts: z.strictObject({ /* same eight keys, nonnegative ints */ }),
});
```
community.lifecycle is z.enum(['active','archived','held','suspended','deletion_pending']) with a refine: only scope 'evidence' may record held, suspended, or deletion_pending (evidence records the state before the takedown); owner/personal report held as 'archived' (as version 1). Row schemas (one strict schema per file kind, exported for import): version 1 row shapes (as CommunityExportManifestV1Schema pins them) plus: entries gain `removal: 'author'|'moderator'|'host'|'erased'|null` (from removed_by / erased_at); attachments camelCase as v1 with archivePath `files/<id>/<sanitized name>`; channelMembers {channel_id, member_id, joined_at}; agentChannelMembers {channel_id, agent_id, joined_at}; members keep email (LEFT JOIN "user") for owner/evidence, only the requester's own for personal. manifest.json at most 1 MiB. Version 1 is no longer written.

### Consistency and rebuild
At start (one short transaction): watermark = max(seq) per exported channel (personal: channels the member can read now); start_redaction_id = max(entry_redactions.id) for the community or 0; verified_content_version = community_content_versions.version. Data segments read messages with seq <= watermark in keyset pages of 1,000, with mentions and files, in short transactions. The collection segments are written after the last data segment from one REPEATABLE READ transaction read in keyset pages (names, roles, memberships as of completion and mutually consistent), and are rewritten on every rebuild pass.
The rule relied on (single-delete spec "Invariant"): a change to an existing entry bumps the version THEN writes an entry_redactions row; a bump with no row is allowed only for export deletions and member/agent changes (read fresh by the collection segments). Each data segment stores content_digest = SHA-256 over its entries' (id, payload_hash, removed_at, erased_at) and its file ids, computed when written. Scope: a text rewrite that keeps payload_hash (erasure's mention rewrite on other people's entries keeps it on purpose) is NOT caught by the digest and relies on its redaction row; the digest is a safety net for removals and file changes. Before the tail: (1) read v = version; (2) if v != verified_content_version, read entry_redactions with id > last_checked_redaction_id joined to (channel_id, seq); map each to the data segment whose range contains it (ignore rows above the watermark); rewrite those segments from current rows (new blob, old queued for deletion); (3) unexplained change: v moved but step 2 found no row → recompute every data segment's content_digest from the database and rewrite each segment whose digest differs; (4) store verified_content_version = v and last_checked_redaction_id; repeat at most 5 passes, then fail EXPORT_CONTENT_CHANGING. A file whose attachments row or blob disappears between page read and streaming (BLOB_NOT_FOUND or missing row) = a content change: discard the segment in progress and rewrite it from current rows (counts as a pass). The tail's final transaction reads `SELECT version FROM community_content_versions WHERE community_id=$1 FOR SHARE` and commits only if equal to verified_content_version; else back to (1), counted as a pass.

### Job model (export_archives becomes job + archive)
States queued → building → ready → (expired via sweep); failed; cancelled.
- POST /me/export and POST /owner/export (owner: password reauth unchanged) insert queued and answer 202 { export }; while an open one exists (queued/building/ready unexpired) for the same scope and requester (personal) or community (owner), answer 200 { export } with it. Lifecycles unchanged: personal active; owner active, archived, held.
- Worker src/export-worker.ts started from main.ts: claim with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, 5-minute lease renewed after each segment, at most COMMUNITY_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY jobs per replica. A dead replica's job resumes from the last committed segment; an uncommitted reservation goes through existing cleanup.
- Before each segment re-check the requester (owner: still owner; personal: can still read each exported channel) and lifecycle; else failed EXPORT_ACCESS_ENDED, segments queued for deletion.
- Each segment: reserveManagedBlob(…, 'export', { allowArchived: scope === 'owner' }); blobStore.put kind 'export_segment'; commit blob + export_segments row in one transaction. At most one staged segment per running job.
- Deadline COMMUNITY_EXPORT_MAX_HOURS from claim → failed EXPORT_TIMED_OUT.
- Ready: ready_at, expires_at = now + COMMUNITY_EXPORT_TTL_HOURS, byte_size = sum of segments, tenant audit export.create.
- POST /exports/:id/cancel by requester in queued/building → cancelled, segments queued. 409 once ready.
- sweepExpiredExports: ready past expires_at → queue every segment (and v1 blob_key); failed/cancelled rows removed 7 days after ending (their segments are queued when they end).
- Exports stay exempt from the storage limit; bytes show in host usage as export bytes.
- scope 'evidence' (takedown spec): no requester; export_archives.evidence_takedown_id set. Authority = the takedown: before each segment check the community_takedowns row exists (state active OR reversed — a reversal does not stop evidence). Any lifecycle while the community row exists (deletion_pending; suspended after reversal); the tenant deletion worker cannot run while that takedown's evidence is pending. Reservations use a new option `reserveManagedBlob(client, id, 'export', { evidence: takedownId })` accepting any lifecycle and recording managed_blobs.evidence_takedown_id; prepareManagedBlobCommit for such a reservation checks the takedown row exists instead of comparing lifecycle versions (reversal bumps the version mid-segment). Not subject to the one-open rule, requester checks, listing, or download. Manifest community.lifecycle = the state before the takedown.

### Config (src/config.ts)
COMMUNITY_EXPORT_SEGMENT_BYTES default 268435456, range 64 MiB–1 GiB; COMMUNITY_EXPORT_TTL_HOURS default 24, 1–168; COMMUNITY_EXPORT_MAX_HOURS default 24, 1–168; COMMUNITY_EXPORT_CONCURRENCY default 1, 1–8.

### Routes and wire (qualified and alias)
POST /me/export, POST /owner/export, GET /exports (open or ended within 7 days), GET /exports/:id (status JSON; previously bytes), GET /exports/:id/archive (bytes), POST /exports/:id/cancel.
```ts
export const CommunityWireExportSchema = z.strictObject({ id, scope: z.enum(['personal','owner']),
  state: z.enum(['queued','building','ready','failed','cancelled','expired']),
  progress: z.strictObject({ done: z.int().nonnegative(), total: z.int().nonnegative().nullable() }), // messages + files
  byteSize: z.int().positive().nullable(),
  failureCode: z.enum(['EXPORT_TIMED_OUT','EXPORT_ACCESS_ENDED','EXPORT_CONTENT_CHANGING','EXPORT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE']).nullable(),
  createdAt: timestamp, readyAt: timestamp.nullable(), expiresAt: timestamp.nullable() });
export const CommunityWireExportResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ export: CommunityWireExportSchema });
export const CommunityWireExportListSchema = z.strictObject({ exports: z.array(CommunityWireExportSchema).max(50) });
```
Replaces today's { archiveId, version, createdAt } (only the same-origin browser parses it).
Download GET /exports/:id/archive: only ready, unexpired, requester = caller, same authority as today. Headers Accept-Ranges: bytes; strong ETag "<id>.<ready_at epoch ms>"; Content-Length; Cache-Control private, no-store; downloadHeaders name community-export.zip / my-community-data.zip. Single Range (a-b, a-, -n) → 206 with Content-Range; If-Range mismatch → 200 full; past end → 416; multi-range → 200 full. Map ranges onto segments via the segmented source. Re-check before the first byte and then every 16 MiB or 10 seconds BOTH the requester's authority AND the export row (still exists, state ready, not deleted by erasure or takedown); end the stream with an error when either fails. Version 1 archives (one blob) served the same way.

### Erasure
erasure.ts deleteExports: limit to state='ready' rows; in the same transaction SELECT every segment blob_key of those exports (and any v1 blob_key) and queue them BEFORE deleting the rows (deleting first cascades export_segments away and loses the keys). applyHusk's leftover check `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM export_archives WHERE community_id=$1 AND deleted_at IS NULL)` (~L486 on #2029) becomes `… AND state='ready' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, else a queued/building job makes the husk answer 'again' forever. Jobs in progress are left to the rebuild.

### Migration
export_archives: format_version int NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK IN (1,2) (internal; not on the wire); evidence_takedown_id uuid NULL set exactly when scope='evidence'; managed_blobs.evidence_takedown_id uuid NULL; state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ready' CHECK IN ('queued','building','ready','failed','cancelled'); blob_key nullable with CHECK ((format_version=1) = (blob_key IS NOT NULL)); byte_size and expires_at nullable with CHECK ((state='ready') = (byte_size IS NOT NULL AND expires_at IS NOT NULL)); scope check adds 'evidence'; requester_member_id nullable with CHECK ((scope='evidence') = (requester_member_id IS NULL)); watermark jsonb, start_redaction_id bigint, last_checked_redaction_id bigint, verified_content_version bigint, rebuild_passes int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, progress counters, lease_until, attempts, next_attempt_at, deadline_at, ready_at, failure_code (pattern ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$); partial unique indexes: one open owner export per community, one open personal export per requester.
export_segments(export_id uuid REFERENCES export_archives(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, segment_no int >0, kind CHECK IN ('data','collection','tail'), blob_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE, byte_size bigint >0, first_channel_id uuid, first_seq bigint, last_channel_id uuid, last_seq bigint (set exactly when kind='data'), entries_index bytea NOT NULL, content_digest text NOT NULL, entry_count int, file_count int, created_at, PRIMARY KEY (export_id, segment_no)). Mirror in schema.ts. Add an ops script `exports:purge-v2` (queues v2 segments and deletes v2 rows) for backout.

### Browser (Manage.tsx, CommunityAdministration.tsx)
Owner: "Export this community" → password → "We're preparing your export. A large community can take a while. You can close this page; we'll keep going." Progress bar from polling GET /exports/:id every 5 s (progress.done of progress.total; indeterminate while total is null). Ready: "Download (<size>)" + "Available until <date, time>." Failure sentences: EXPORT_TIMED_OUT "This export took too long and stopped. Try again."; EXPORT_ACCESS_ENDED "Your access changed while we were preparing it."; EXPORT_CONTENT_CHANGING "The community kept changing while we were preparing it. Try again later."; EXPORT_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE "We couldn't store the export. Try again later." with Try again; Cancel while preparing. Member "Download my data": same states. Help text: "The export is a .zip. It has your community's messages, files, members, and settings. Messages posted after the export starts aren't included. Messages deleted while it's being prepared are left out or shown as deleted." Phone/tablet/desktop.

### Docs
API.md (routes, range behaviour, manifest v2 format), OPERATIONS.md (settings, disk sizing = one segment per concurrent job, export storage and lifetime), docs/guides/communities.mdx, changelog fragment.

### Acceptance criteria (real Postgres, both BlobStores, purpose comment each)
- AC-1: 12,000 messages in one channel, 11,000 members, 1.2 GiB of sparse synthetic files, segment size 64 MiB: owner export reaches ready; more than one data segment; yauzl and our reader list every entry; every message, member, file present once; file bytes hash to checksums.
- AC-3: staging directory never holds more than one segment per running job (sampled after each segment); worker heap under 256 MiB.
- AC-4: kill after first data segment and again during the tail; another worker finishes; archive byte-identical to an uninterrupted run; no orphan export blob after cleanup.
- AC-5: a message posted after start is absent; a member renamed after start appears with the new name.
- AC-6: after segment 2 of 4, delete a message in segment 1 and erase a member whose messages are in segment 3 (hooks): archive has tombstones and husk; segments 2 and 4 blob keys unchanged; rebuild_passes = 1.
- AC-7: a removal committed between the last check and the final FOR SHARE read makes the tail go round again; a removal waiting on that lock commits after ready and (erasure) deletes the export; 5 passes of changes → EXPORT_CONTENT_CHANGING, no segment after cleanup.
- AC-6b: a hook deletes a file row of segment 2 with a version bump and no redaction row → the archive omits the file, segment 2 rewritten via the digest check, others unchanged; a file whose blob disappears mid-segment (hook) → the segment is rewritten and the job finishes.
- AC-10b: with an owner export building, an erasure completes (husk step does not loop), the job rebuilds; a ready export present at the same time is deleted with every segment blob queued (pending_delete, none orphaned).
- AC-8: three Range requests (start, middle across a segment boundary, end) concatenated = SHA-256 of one full download; If-Range wrong ETag → 200 full; bytes=<size>- → 416; multi-range → 200 full; demoting the owner mid-download ends the stream within 16 MiB; an erasure or takedown deleting the export mid-download ends the stream within 16 MiB and a following ranged request answers 404.
- AC-9: manifest.json last before the central directory, parses with V2 schema; every NDJSON line parses; counts match; name, description, admission policy, icon bytes+checksum present; memberships match tables; removed entry removal 'author', erased 'erased'; files named files/<id>/<sanitized>; a file named ../../evil stored without slashes.
- AC-10: second request while building → same export 200; ready export expires after TTL (clock) and sweep deletes segments; cancel while building leaves no segment.
- AC-11: demoting the owner while building → EXPORT_ACCESS_ENDED before the next segment; personal export requester leaving a channel → same.
- AC-12: COMMUNITY_EXPORT_MAX_HOURS=1 with clock past → EXPORT_TIMED_OUT, segments queued.
- AC-13: community B's rows and blobs never read by A's export.
- Erasure suites (#2029) pass with deleteExports handling segments; browser tests render states at three widths.

tasks.description:
Make import (host-operator P3, tasks 4.1/4.2, migration 0016) read version 1 and version 2 archives of any size, uploaded in resumable parts. Depends on host-operator task 4.2 and tasks 1.1/1.2 here. Migration: the next free number at build time.

### Reader and dispatch
Replace fflate's streaming Unzip in the import worker with src/archive/zip-reader.ts (task 1.1) over a segmented source of the uploaded parts (or the single-PUT staging blob). Read manifest.json through the central directory. version 1 → P3 rules unchanged (manifest first, attachments/<uuid> names, 10,000-row and 16 MiB limits, single restore transaction). version 2 → rules below. Other → IMPORT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. scope other than owner → IMPORT_NOT_OWNER_EXPORT. CommunityAdminImportReportSchema.manifestVersion accepts 1 | 2.

### Validate (version 2)
Stream every NDJSON file in manifest order; parse each line with its strict row schema (exported from @dorkos/shared/community-wire by task 1.2); compare counts with the manifest; stream every file and compare length and SHA-256 with its metadata row; check the storage limit against the sum. Allowed names: manifest.json, the tail file names, entries/NNNNNN.ndjson, attachments/NNNNNN.ndjson, files/<uuid>/<name without slash>, community/icon. Referential checks the database cannot express (a mention resolves to exactly one member or agent of this import; a thread root is not a reply) run per batch during restore with indexed lookups.

### Restore (version 2)
Batches of up to 1,000 rows in dependency order (channels, members, handles, agents, channel memberships, entries per channel in seq order, mentions, attachments, audit), each batch its own transaction, derived IDs (uuidv5(importId, sourceId)) and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, progress recorded, so a restarted worker resumes. The community stays pending_owner with no member; the final transaction commits reserved blobs, sets imported_at, marks the job ready; failure → existing abandon path. Beyond version 1, restore: description when the create request gave none (host-supplied name always wins), admission policy when the create request gave none, the icon, removal markers (removed_by, or erased_at for 'erased'), and the adopted owner's own channel memberships (version 1 or an owner with none → every channel). Other people's memberships are not restored (their rows are historical).

### Parts upload (beside P3's single PUT, unchanged at most 1 GiB)
Authorized by the upload token or host authority with communities:import:
- PUT /api/v1/imports/:importId/archive/parts/:partNumber (1–10,000), body ≤ COMMUNITY_EXPORT_SEGMENT_BYTES, headers Content-Length and X-Part-SHA256; each part a managed blob purpose 'import_staging'; same part+hash → 200 no write; different hash replaces it (before complete). In-flight limits: at most 4 part uploads at once per import and COMMUNITY_IMPORT_PART_CONCURRENCY (default 8, 1–64) per replica; beyond either answer 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After: 5 before reading the body (local disk for imports ≤ concurrency × part size). Bypasses the JSON body buffer in app.ts like the attachment route.
- GET /api/v1/imports/:importId/archive/parts → received part numbers, sizes, hashes.
- POST /api/v1/imports/:importId/archive/complete { parts, archiveBytes, archiveSha256 }: parts must be exactly 1..parts; stream in order computing SHA-256; mismatch → discard every part, 400 IMPORT_ARCHIVE_INVALID, token stays valid in its window; success spends the token and moves the job to validating.
- archiveBytes ≤ COMMUNITY_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES (default 1 GiB, max 1 TiB) else 413 IMPORT_TOO_LARGE. Upload window COMMUNITY_IMPORT_UPLOAD_HOURS (default 24, 1–168).
Migration: community_import_parts(import_id, part_number, blob_key UNIQUE, byte_size, sha256, PRIMARY KEY (import_id, part_number)); community_imports.upload_kind CHECK IN ('single','parts'); version 2 restore progress columns. Mirror in schema.ts. Wire additions in packages/shared/src/community-admin-wire.ts for the part list and complete request.

### Docs
API.md import section (parts, version 2), OPERATIONS.md (the two settings), changelog fragment.

### Acceptance criteria
- AC-14: seed A with removed and erased messages, private channels, an icon, 12,000 messages; export v2 (64 MiB segments); upload in parts to another community on the same host, killing the upload after two parts and resuming from GET …/parts; complete; validate; commit; claim. Counts, text, thread shape, tombstones, removal markers, file bytes, icon, description, and the owner's own channel memberships match through the ID map. A version 1 archive from a real version 1 export still imports through the new reader (P3 round trip unchanged). Tampered v2 archives fail with the named code and leave nothing after cleanup: changed file byte (IMPORT_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH), NDJSON line failing its schema, count mismatch, duplicate name, name with '..', entry inflating past its declared size (IMPORT_ARCHIVE_INVALID), version 3 (IMPORT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED). An archive above COMMUNITY_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES → 413 IMPORT_TOO_LARGE at complete. A worker killed mid-restore resumes and finishes with each row once. A fifth concurrent part upload to one import, and uploads beyond COMMUNITY_IMPORT_PART_CONCURRENCY on a replica, answer 429 with Retry-After before reading the body.

tasks.description:
Let the DorkOS app move a community of any size: publish an additive `parts` field on the move upload in packages/cloud-api (contract first, its own PR, label `cloud-contract`), then use it in the DorkOS app's move flow. Depends on task 2.1 and host-operator task 5.2 (the move flow). Nothing private goes in this repo (no prices, plan names, hostnames).

### Contract (packages/cloud-api/src/communities.ts)
`CommunityMoveUploadSchema` gains
```ts
parts: z.object({
  partBytes: z.number().int().positive().describe('The largest part the upload accepts.'),
  maxBytes: z.number().int().positive().describe('The largest file a parted upload accepts.'),
}).optional().describe('Present when the Community server accepts the file in parts.'),
```
Doc comment: when present, the app may upload a file up to parts.maxBytes in parts of at most partBytes with PUT `${url}/parts/{n}` (headers Content-Length, X-Part-SHA256, bearer token), list received parts with GET `${url}/parts`, and finish with POST `${url}/complete` { parts, archiveBytes, archiveSha256 }; a whole-file digest mismatch at complete discards every part and the token stays usable until expiresAt. `maxBytes` keeps meaning the largest file a single PUT accepts. Additive and optional per the package's rule; conformance fixtures with and without `parts`; the catalog-blindness test stays green. packages/cloud-api/README.md mentions it.

### DorkOS app (host-operator 5.2's move flow, apps/server local routes under /api/cloud/communities/* and the client dialog)

When absent: the single PUT as today (files over maxBytes refused client-side as today). The determinate progress bar counts bytes across parts. The browser never sees the token.
